text:
maya: Heads up — after the NF4 rollout to canary region eu-west-1 we see a sharp throughput drop for text-generation routes (~30% P50->P50) and intermittent OOM-ish memory spikes on a subset of pods. Root logs attached below.

jorge: ugh, saw a few alerts, thanks for flagging. Is this any particular model or all NF4-backed endpoints?

maya: Primarily the T5-family endpoints we converted last night. FP4 endpoints look stable. Repro on canary: loadtest at 200rps produces throughput collapse after ~60s. Sample logs:

maya: ```
[2026-03-18T09:33:01Z] serve: kernel_load: nf4_gemm_v2 selected for layer 12
[2026-03-18T09:33:04Z] batching: reduced batch size from 32->6 due to kv-mem-pressure
[2026-03-18T09:33:05Z] kvcache: eviction triggered: evicted 120 entries (~48MB)
[2026-03-18T09:33:06Z] mem: RSS jump 2.1GB -> 6.8GB; oom_protector triggered
[2026-03-18T09:33:07Z] serve: kernel switch: nf4_gemm_v2 -> fallback_int8 (latency penalty)
```

olga: can you paste the pprof flamegraph or perf record? want to see if kernel selection churn is to blame or allocator fragmentation.

maya: attached a lightweight profile: CPU sampling shows lots of time in our kernel selector and nvalloc. pprof excerpt:

maya: ```
Top functions:
  kernel_selector::score_variant 35.2%
  nv_alloc::allocate 23.6%
  continuous_batcher::split_batch 12.9%
  nf4_gemm_v2::exec 8.1%
```

sam: kernel_selector being 35% is suspicious — are we recalculating per-request instead of per-model/seq-length bucket? there was a change last week to re-evaluate on token horizon.

jorge: correct — PR #492 added a token-horizon-aware scoring so selector runs more often. It was meant to help dynamic batching but maybe too aggressive for small models.

lee: I remember we scoped that to only run when seq_len changes >32. Did the condition regress? logs show many evaluations even though seq_len steady at 128.

maya: looks like the caching key for selector includes a floating calibration score (from NF4 calibration pass). calibration_score varies slightly each request (non-deterministic float). That makes the selector cache miss every time -> repeated kernel selection -> nvalloc churn -> KV eviction.

olga: that matches memory churn. If kernel selection picks different kernels, our kernel init path allocates temporary buffers per kernel which aren't reused due to affinity mapping. Also NVML shows pagealloc spikes aligned to kernel switch.

sam: so root cause hypothesis: calibration float jitter included in selector cache key -> cache miss storm -> kernel-switch churn -> allocations -> kv cache eviction -> reduced effective batch sizes -> throughput drop.

jorge: solid. Does this only affect NF4 kernels? why FP4 didn't show same behavior?

maya: NF4 calibration code appends per-layer scale stats as a float array to the model profile object. FP4 saved quant params deterministically as ints. So FP4 cache key stable.

lee: quick mitigation — revert selector to ignore calibration floats (or quantize them) and force reuse for same model+seq_len. We can also pin kernel affinity for a short window (e.g., 10s) to avoid rapid switching.

olga: agree. Also increase kvcache bucket retention threshold during canary to avoid evictions while we test.

ci-bot: rollout: revert-kernel-selector-cache-key-change -> started on canary at 09:48Z by @sam

maya: after the revert we re-ran loadtest, initial results look promising: no RSS spikes and stable throughput at baseline. Numbers: P50 before fix 120ms -> after fix 95ms (baseline 90ms). throughput restored to ~95% of original.

jorge: nice. We should still patch selector to quantize calibration values (e.g., round to 3 decimals) and update unit tests to assert cache key stability. Also add telemetry for cache miss rate per-model.

sam: creating followups:
- action/1 @jorge: PR to quantize calibration floats in profile cache key (due EOD)
- action/2 @lee: add kernel-affinity cooldown of 10s and make it configurable (due tomorrow)
- action/3 @olga: bump kvcache eviction threshold for canary and add metric (done)
- action/4 @maya: gather pprof traces and perf counters for the pod during the incident and upload to S3 (due EOD)

olga: I'm adding a regression test in perf-harness that simulates jittered calibration metadata to ensure we don't blow cache hit rate to zero.

maya: also found one minor alloc bug: nf4_gemm_v2::init does a temp cudaMalloc without free on error path; will patch in same PR.

infra-bot: deploy revert-kernel-selector-cache-key-change succeeded on 4/4 canary pods at 09:52Z

maya: confirming stable for the last 15m, closing incident unless anyone objects. thanks all :tada:

jorge: i'll follow up with a short postmortem and link to the PRs + perf graphs.

lee: thumbs up. we should also add a lint that flags non-deterministic pieces in cache keys.

maya: final note: lesson learned — avoid putting high-entropy floating vectors in cache keys. prefer quantized/int summaries.
